---
title: "Feature Normalization under Finite Training Budgets"
description: >
  How feature standardization changes the trade-off between learning rare
  effects and amplifying noise in stochastic gradient descent with limited data.
author:
  - Johan Larsson
abstract: >
  Feature scaling affects both how quickly stochastic gradient descent learns
  rare effects and how much noise it accumulates. We compare standardized and
  unscaled training under a shared observation budget, allowing each method to
  choose its learning rate and stopping time. For two independent binary
  features, we characterize the best attainable risk on the rare subgroup as its
  prevalence decreases. The preferred scaling depends on how the signal is
  distributed between the common and rare features, as well as on the noise and
  available budget. Further bounds and experiments examine finite prevalence,
  reused observations, estimated preprocessing, and fitted intercepts. We also
  show that selecting a predictor after training can reverse the comparison.
